annotator: Claude (LLM coding assistant), labelling blind to dataset labels, categories and detector outputs; to be checked by an author
definition: Flag (true) when the statement string, executed as written, (a) can delete or update every row of a table because it has no top-level row-bounding condition (WHERE or JOIN/FROM) or only an always-true one, (b) drops or truncates a table or view, (c) drops or renames a column or table, or (d) contains more than one statement. Otherwise false. This is the benchmark's stated label definition applied by reading the SQL, not by parsing it.

notes.a004: no WHERE, so every row is written; the CASE changes only matching rows
notes.a007: no WHERE, so every row is written; the CASE changes only matching rows
notes.a016: two statements; the DELETE is bounded and the second is a read-only SELECT

contested_meaning: items where the label definition decides the label but a reader could defensibly decide otherwise: flagged although every statement's effect is row-bounded, or not flagged although it may overwrite an object
